column3: Insurance costs rise > wages → Affordability pressure → Consumers reduce coverage, raise deductibles, OR lapse policies → Uninsured/underinsured exposure grows → Loss event triggers financial crisis → Debt cascade
column4: Insurance is non-discretionary but priced at actuarial necessity. Consumer income doesn't adjust. Gap between actuarial necessity and affordability creates systematic underinsurance. Auto (mandatory) = first lapse signal.
column5: Premium increases drive lapses; lapses worsen risk pool via adverse selection; adverse selection drives further premium increases
column6: Premium growth exceeds wage growth for 3+ consecutive years (CONFIRMED — auto 64% cumulative 2020-2025)
column7: CARL (consumer discretionary spending), GIG (auto = mandatory cost for gig workers)
column11: Auto premium growth >8% sustained; HH income growth <5%
column13: Auto premiums 5.9% YoY (moderating) but 64% cumulative. Affordability destroyed at bottom 40%.

column3: Climate losses → Carrier exits → Non-renewals → Consumers forced to FAIR Plan (higher cost) OR remain uninsured → Force-placed coverage by lender → Housing payment spike → Mortgage stress → Default risk
column4: Climate risk repricing faster than actuarial models. Private withdrawal accelerates as cat losses mount. FAIR Plans were designed as backstop, not primary insurer — overwhelmed by structural private failure.
column5: Residual market growth increases state exposure; assessments from FAIR Plan losses → higher premiums for ALL insured in state; adverse selection in remaining private market
column6: Private market share drops below 50% in major state; OR FAIR Plan assessment > state fiscal capacity
column7: CARL (housing stress), REGINALD (bank exposure to CA real estate)
column9: 30-90 days for non-renewal impact; 12-24 months for property value impact

column3: Health costs increase → High deductibles reduce effective coverage → Medical event occurs → Out-of-pocket exceeds household ability to pay → Medical debt accumulates → Collections → Credit score damage → Bankruptcy risk
column4: HDHPs shifted cost burden to consumers who cannot absorb it. Medical debt is unexpected, catastrophic, and not chosen — unlike mortgage or CC debt. Leading cause of US bankruptcies.
column5: Medical debt reduces credit access; reduced credit increases medical debt risk; CFPB rule vacated = debt stays on reports forever
column6: Medical event exceeds household liquid savings (median ~$5K) for underinsured consumer
column7: CARL (CC DQ, bankruptcy), GIG (gig workers disproportionate OOP exposure)
column11: Medical event for consumer with HDHP deductible >$5K or uninsured
column13: $195B total debt; 62% of bankruptcies; CFPB rule vacated Jul 2025. ACA cliff adding new uninsured to exposure.

column13: CONFIRMED: 1.2M dropped ACA coverage Jan 2026. OBBBA Medicaid: structural 2026-2034 pipeline.
